answer: At dawn, every new agent must pass a comet test: it locks a small stake and earns trust only through slow, verifiable work over time, so identities cannot be minted in bulk. A sybil swarm collapses at its nadir because each fake must fund its own stake and wait out the same proving period, while one honest agent pays once and keeps trading. Fast creation is worthless when reputation is earned at the speed of proof, not the speed of copying.
